bioprojects.title: NHGRI Large Scale Sequencing Program for Organismal Sequencing

assembly_info.comments:
Background: Leishmania arabica LEM1108 (WHO strain identifier MPSA/SA/83/JISH220) was obtained from Professeurs Jean-Pierre Dedet and Patrick Bastien, University Montepellier, France. Genomic DNA was prepared from nuclei isolated from parasites lysed using 0.5% NP-40, to minimize the amount of kinetoplast (mitochondrial) DNA, and was provided by Drs. Deborah E Dobson and Stephen M. Beverley, Washington University School of Medicine. Total sequence coverage of Illumina instrument reads was 187X (fragments, 3 and 8kb) using a genome size estimate of 35Mb. The combined sequence reads were assembled using the ALLPATHS software (Broad Institute). This draft assembly was referred to as Leishmania arabica LEM1108 1.0.3. This version has been gap filled and cleaned of contaminating contigs, and the scaffolds were arranged into chromosomes. The assembly is made up of a total of 36 scaffolds with an N50 scaffold length of over 1.0Mb (N50 contig length was 52kb). The assembly spans 30.6Mb.
This work was supported by NIH grant AI29646 to SMB and by NIH-NHGRI grant 5U54HG00307907 to RKW, Director of The Genome Institute at Washington University.
For questions regarding this Leishmania arabica LEM1108 1.0.3 assembly please contact Dr. Wesley Warren, Washington University School of Medicine (wwarren@genome.wustl.edu). Downloads of the sequence data are available via the TriTrypDB genome browser server. Funding for the sequence characterization of the Leishmania arabica LEM1108 genome was provided by the National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI), National Institutes of Health (NIH).
Source DNA can be obtained by mailing: Stephen M. Beverley, Ph.D. Marvin A. Brennecke Professor and Head of Molecular Microbiology Department of Molecular Microbiology Campus Box 8230 Washington University School of Medicine 660 S. Euclid Ave. St. Louis, MO 63110 USA
